newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed on Wednesday after a volatile session which saw early gains give way to a spasm of retail profit-taking before the return of buyers during the afternoon.

The AEX index closed 0.35 points up at 975.31 after a session which saw it climb to 981.30 fuelled by a big overnight gain on Wall Street before buckling to 956.86 as retail investors clamoured briefly to cash in profits.
"Around midday it got a bit hectic. A lot of retail investors who have got involved in the recent rally got nervous and started to sell," said one trader.
The dealer added that soon after the midsession dip other buyers, convinced that the bull run still has further to go, emerged to pick up bargains.

Others said the firm bond market and dollar had given foreign investors the incentive to buy following Tuesday's 18 point AEX drop. "There's not a lot of domestic institutional involvement, but some foreign players are looking at Tuesday's fall as an opportunity to buy," one dealer said.
Dealers said concern was emerging ahead of Thursday's Dutch central bank money market liquidity announcement, at which it could signal higher interest rates to support the guilder.
"The guilder has been weak against other European currencies and the Dutch central bank might move to increase interest rates to support it, that's hurt the market," said a dealer.

Disappointing first half results from chemicals firm DSM also dented sentiment and held back the AEX, which earlier in the week had climbed strongly in anticipation that cyclical stocks would come up with solid first half numbers.

DSM closed 18.50 guilders or 8.04 percent lower at 211.50, losing ground after news first half net profit rose 13 percent to 465 million guilders, at the lower end of a 452-544 million range of analysts' expectations.
"The DSM figures have got people wondering whether the results from Akzo (due on Thursday morning) will be as good as people were expecting," the dealer said.

Akzo plunged to a session low of 295.00 guilders after the DSM news but rallied to close 0.50 guilders off at 302.50. The shares have risen from 270 guilders since the beginning of July to a peak of 310 guilders on Tuesday, partly fuelled by expectations of a strong rise in first half profits on Thursday.
Shares in airline KLM jumped 2.10 guilders to 74.50 following news it was to sell its 19 percent stake in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines and strengthen their alliance.

KLM said the sale, in four annual tranches between 1997 and 2000, would raise between $1.07 billion and $1.17 billion, while the closer links between the companies would boost synergies and enhance the earnings of both airlines.
"We think it's pretty bullish," said one dealer, adding, "It's slightly more than we had expected and it means KLM can get on with looking for a European partner."

Other leaders saw PolyGram climb 3.50 guilders to 109.50, boosted by talk of a positive broker's note and reports that its "Bean" movie has been well received. Royal Dutch closed 3.40 guilders higher at 115.00. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
